title: Checking calibration and how much to verify
text: Describe design can afford: number sites, automated occasions, fraction sites verified, plausible detection false-positive rates. Describe false-positive structure suspect: homogeneous, random among sites, tracking environmental gradient. Run fp_calibrate() candidate models. Read coverage bias quantity care , usually occupancy slope. replicate costs one Stan fit per model, design needs 3 cells × 50 replicates × 2 models = 300 fits. 50 replicates, Monte Carlo standard error coverage 0.95 0.03, enough tell calibrated model broken one; raise reps pin borderline value. Every model fitted datasets, comparisons models paired.
code: library(crywolf) fp_compile()   # compile once before starting parallel workers  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 8)  design <- expand.grid(   nsite = 300, nocc = 20, p10 = 0.05, frac_verified = 0.3,   conf_effect = c(0, 0.5, 1.5), conf_cor = 0.7 )  cal <- fp_calibrate(   design,   models = list(constant = ~ 1, fp_on_x = ~ x),   occ = ~ x, reps = 50, parallel = TRUE ) summary(cal)

title: Checking calibration and how much to verify
text: Verification anchors false-positive rate. natural think verifying sites rescue model calibrated, fp_verification_curve() tests directly:
code: fp_verification_curve(   nsite = 300, nocc = 20, p10 = 0.05, conf_effect = 1.5, conf_cor = 0.7,   frac_verified = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9),   models = list(constant = ~ 1, fp_on_x = ~ x),   reps = 50, parallel = TRUE )

title: Checking calibration and how much to verify
text: simulation study motivated package (Provete et al., preparation), base false-positive rate 0.05: false positives homogeneous varied random among sites, constant-rate model kept nominal coverage occupancy slope. false-positive rate tracked gradient correlated occupancy covariate (effect 1.5 logit scale, correlation 0.7), coverage slope fell 0.08–0.20, verifying 90% sites restore . Letting false-positive rate depend occupancy covariate (fp = ~ x) recovered part coverage (0.48–0.66) improved verification; true gradient (fp = ~ w), coverage returned 0.90–0.97. Weak confusion (effects 0.5 less) left constant-rate model calibrated every correlation, including false positives depended occupancy covariate . , fp_verification_curve() shows constant-rate model stuck nominal coverage, verifying remedy. Model false-positive rate instead, verify enough tell effect apart occupancy effect.

title: Checking calibration and how much to verify
code: library(ggplot2) s <- summary(cal) ggplot(subset(s, parameter == "occ_x"),        aes(conf_effect, coverage, colour = model)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, linetype = 2) +   geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = coverage - 2 * mc_se, ymax = coverage + 2 * mc_se),                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.1)) +   labs(x = "Confusion effect (logit scale)",        y = "Coverage of the 95% interval of the occupancy slope") +   theme_classic()

title: crywolf: Bayesian false-positive occupancy models with calibration checks — crywolf-package
text: site \(\), automated occasion \(k\), verified occasion \(m\): $$z_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\psi_i), \quad \mathrm{logit}(\psi_i) = X_i\beta$$ $$y^{aut}_{ik} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(z_i p_{11,ik} + (1 - z_i) p_{10,})$$ $$\mathrm{logit}(p_{11,ik}) = Z_{ik}\alpha + u_{j[ik]}, \quad       \mathrm{logit}(p_{10,}) = \alpha_1 - \Delta + W_i\gamma$$ $$y^{ver}_{im} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(z_i r_{11})$$ latent state \(z\) marginalized. positive gap \(\Delta\) keeps true-detection probability false-positive probability reference values covariates, prevents label switching.

title: Posterior predictive check for a false-positive occupancy model — fp_ppc
text: latent occupancy state marginalized Stan model, posterior draw \(z_i\) first drawn conditional posterior given data parameters, $$\Pr(z_i = 1 \mid \mathbf{y}_i, \theta) = \frac{\psi_i\, f(\mathbf{y}_i \mid z_i = 1, \theta)}{\psi_i\, f(\mathbf{y}_i \mid z_i = 1, \theta) + (1 - \psi_i)\, f(\mathbf{y}_i \mid z_i = 0, \theta)},$$ 1 sites verified detection. Given \(z_i\), automated detections replicated probability \(z_i p_{11} + (1 - z_i) p_{10}\) verified detections probability \(z_i r_{11}\). discrepancy computed observed replicated data \(z\) parameters, Bayesian p-value proportion draws replicated discrepancy exceeds observed one. Values near 0 1 indicate lack fit; values near 0.5 indicate observed data typical fitted model. p-value near 0.5 show false-positive process correctly specified: check detection counts can little power false-positive rate tracks unmeasured gradient. Use fp_calibrate() ask whether intervals given model calibrated design. elements y yrep follow conventions 'bayesplot' package, ppc_*() functions can used directly, example bayesplot::ppc_bars(ppc$y, ppc$yrep).
